findings.what: The chat-list layout preference is implemented twice, with two different NSUserDefaults keys and two different value types. Settings owns `static NSString *const TGSettingsChatListLayoutKey = @"TGChatListLayout";` (line 72) and stores an NSString "a"/"b" via +setChatListLayout: (line 763-772). The chat list owns `static NSString *const TGChatListFolderStyleKey = @"TGChatListFolderStyle";` (TGChatListViewController.m:481) and reads an NSInteger 0/1 via TGChatListFolderStyle() (TGChatListViewController.m:497-500).
findings.failure: User opens Settings -> Chat List Layout and taps "Chooser in the Title". +setChatListLayout: writes @"a" under key "TGChatListLayout" and posts TGSettingsChatListLayoutChangedNotification. Nothing reads that key and nothing observes that notification (grep for both names returns only TGSettingsViewController.m). TGChatListFolderStyle() still reads "TGChatListFolderStyle", finds nothing, and returns the TGChatListFolderStyleStrip default. The chat list never changes, and the checkmark in Settings does move, so the setting looks applied and is completely inert.
findings.fix: Delete the parallel implementation in TGSettingsViewController.m: remove TGSettingsChatListLayoutKey (line 72), TGSettingsChatListLayoutChangedNotification (lines 81-82), +chatListLayout/+chatListLayoutTitle/+setChatListLayout: (lines 746-772). Make +chatListLayout read and +setChatListLayout: write the integer key @"TGChatListFolderStyle" using the values TGChatListFolderStyleChooser=0 / TGChatListFolderStyleStrip=1 defined at TGChatListViewController.m:483-484, keeping the existing title array order (index 0 = Chooser, index 1 = Strip). Move those two constants plus TGChatListFolderStyle() into a shared header so both files use one definition, and have TGChatListViewController observe the change notification and call -reloadData.

findings.what: The "show stories" preference is implemented twice under two different keys. Settings: `static NSString *const TGSettingsStoriesEnabledKey = @"TGStoriesEnabled";` written by +setStoriesEnabled: (line 725) and read by +storiesEnabled (line 717). Chat list: `static NSString *const TGChatListStoriesTrayKey = @"TGShowStoriesTray";` (TGChatListViewController.m:481-480) read by TGStoriesTrayEnabled() (TGChatListViewController.m:493-495), which is the only gate on the tray (used at lines 937, 1191, 1590).
findings.failure: Turning the Stories switch off writes NO to "TGStoriesEnabled". TGStoriesTrayEnabled() reads "TGShowStoriesTray", which no code in src/ ever writes, so `stored` is nil and it returns the YES default forever. The stories tray stays on screen (and keeps downloading story avatars, ~82pt of the chat list and a per-poster file download on a 512MB device) no matter what the user chooses. Symmetrically, TGSettingsStoriesEnabledChangedNotification (line 79-80) has no observers.
findings.fix: Pick one key. Simplest: change TGSettingsStoriesEnabledKey (TGSettingsViewController.m:71) to @"TGShowStoriesTray" so +storiesEnabled/+setStoriesEnabled: and TGStoriesTrayEnabled() agree, and make +storiesEnabled default to YES when the key is absent (it currently defaults from `objectForKey:` with no default, line 717-719) so both sides agree on the unset case. Then have TGChatListViewController observe TGSettingsStoriesEnabledChangedNotification and rebuild its header rows.

findings.what: The TDLib message-content -> one-line-label table is written five times with divergent output: TGMessagePreview (TGClient.m:1628-1679), TGSearchPreview (TGClient+Search.m:17-38), TGForumsPreview (TGClient+Forums.m:25-38), TGSavedPreview (TGClient+SavedMessages.m:37-49), -quoteKindLabelFor: (TGChatViewController.m:4134-4154). They disagree: messageDocument is "Document" in three copies and "File" in TGChatViewController.m:4136+ and TGClient+Notifications.m:553; messageAudio is "Audio" in four and "Music" in TGChatViewController.m:4134; messageVenue is handled only in TGClient+SavedMessages.m:47 and TGClient.m:1657. Crucially only TGClient.m's copy ignores the caption: the other four return content[@"caption"][@"text"] first (TGClient+Search.m:11-15, TGClient+Forums.m:19-24, TGClient+SavedMessages.m:28-33).
findings.failure: Send or receive a photo with the caption "see you at 7". The chat list row (which goes through -previewForLastMessage:inChat: -> TGMessagePreview, TGClient.m:2365) shows "Photo", while the identical chat found through search shows "see you at 7". The same message therefore reads differently in two places in the app, and the chat list loses the only information that distinguishes captioned media rows from each other.
findings.fix: Extract one function, e.g. `NSString *TGContentPreview(NSDictionary *content)`, into a shared header (TGClient+Private.h is already imported by every TGClient category). Body: caption-first (guarded isKindOfClass: on content, caption dict and caption[@"text"]), then the union of the five tables using one label per type (settle on "Document", "Audio", and add messageVenue -> "Location" and messageLiveLocation -> "Live location" everywhere), then the TGPhraseFromTypeName fallback from TGClient.m:1678. Replace all five bodies with a call to it.

findings.what: The same four TDLib guard helpers (dict/array/string/isError) are copy-pasted 22 times under 22 different prefixes: TGDict/TGArray/TGString/TGIsError in TGClient+Contacts.m:4-25, TGClient+Groups.m:4-18 and TGClient+Stickers.m:4-27; plus prefixed clones TGAccount* (TGClient+Account.m:4-42), TGAS* (TGClient+AppSettings.m:4-21), TGB* (TGClient+Bots.m:4-22), TGCalls* (TGClient+Calls.m:4-25), TGCh* (TGClient+Channels.m:4-25), TGCM* (TGClient+ChatManagement.m:7-28), TGFiles* (TGClient+Files.m:19-34), TGMC* (TGClient+MessageContent.m:23), TGMsg* (TGClient+Messages.m:4), TGNet* (TGClient+Network.m:26-61), TGNotif* (TGClient+Notifications.m:15-33), TGPay* (TGClient+Payments.m:7), TGPremium* (TGClient+Premium.m:50-78), TGPrivacy* (TGClient+Privacy.m:4-33), TGSc* (TGClient+SecretChats.m:11-26), TGStorage* (TGClient+Storage.m:53), TGStory* (TGClient+Stories.m:4-23), TGTr* (TGClient+Translation.m:4), TGUS* (TGClient+UserStatus.m:22), TGWL* (TGClient+WebLinks.m:4). The contracts contradict each other for the same name: TGString returns @"" in TGClient+Contacts.m:12 and TGClient+Groups.m:12 but nil in TGClient+Stickers.m:17; TGArray returns nil in TGClient+Contacts.m:8 and TGClient+Stickers.m:9 but @[] in TGClient+Groups.m:8. The error predicates also disagree: TGAccountIsError (TGClient+Account.m:8-9) and TGNetIsError (TGClient+Network.m:30-31) return YES when @type is not an NSString, while TGChIsError (TGClient+Channels.m:8), TGTrIsError (TGClient+Translation.m:8) and TGWLIsError (TGClient+WebLinks.m:8) return NO for the same input.
findings.failure: Any agent moving code between two of these files silently changes its behaviour. Concretely: code written against TGClient+Groups.m's contract, e.g. `for (id x in TGArray(v))`, is safe there (@[] on a bad reply) but iterates nil (no-op, silently empty result) if pasted into TGClient+Contacts.m; and `@{ @"title" : TGString(v) }` is safe in TGClient+Groups.m but throws NSInvalidArgumentException ("attempt to insert nil object") in TGClient+Stickers.m, where TGString returns nil. Every current call site in TGClient+Stickers.m happens to write `TGString(...) ?: @""` (lines 60, 97, 98, 456, 507), which is exactly the defensive tax the divergence imposes.
findings.fix: Add one set of `static inline` helpers to src/TGClient+Private.h (already imported by all of these files) with a single documented contract: TGDict -> nil on mismatch, TGArray -> @[] on mismatch, TGString -> @"" on mismatch, TGNumber -> nil, TGInt64 -> longLongValue of NSNumber/NSString else 0, TGIsError -> YES unless the value is an NSDictionary whose @type is an NSString other than @"error". Delete all 22 prefixed copies and rename their call sites. Keep the non-generic helpers (TGNetProxyDict, TGAccountSessionDict, TGWLRichPair etc.) where they are.

findings.what: TGActionsMenuButton (TGActionsMenu.m:26-108) is a near-verbatim copy of TGPopupMenuButton (TGPopupMenu.m:18-104): the same seven UIImageView ivars, the same four `MenuButtonTopLine.png` / `MenuButtonBottomLine.png` / `_Highlighted` loads, the same -applyHighlight:, -setHighlighted:, -setSelected: and -layoutSubviews. The three layout constants are duplicated verbatim too: `kMenuHeight = 41.0f; kMenuTitlePadding = 34.0f; kMenuLineInset = 10.0f;` at TGPopupMenu.m:4-6 and again at TGActionsMenu.m:13-15. Each file also keeps its own open-menu singleton (`static TGPopupMenu *sOpenMenu` TGPopupMenu.m:8, `static TGActionsMenuView *sOpenMenu` TGActionsMenu.m:126) and its own +dismiss.
findings.failure: ~110 lines of pixel-layout code and three metrics exist twice, so a change to the menu card (for example the row height, which drives both the popup card and the actions menu) applied to one file leaves the other at the old value and the two menus in the same screen render at different heights. The two independent singletons also mean neither +dismiss closes the other; TGChatListViewController.m:1122-1123 only works because it happens to call both, and any new call site that calls one will leave the other's full-screen tap-catcher installed.
findings.fix: Move TGPopupMenuButton and the three kMenu* constants into a shared internal header (e.g. TGPopupMenu+Internal.h) and have TGActionsMenu.m use TGPopupMenuButton instead of TGActionsMenuButton; delete TGActionsMenu.m:22-108 and 13-15. Then make one of the two +dismiss methods dismiss both singletons so a single call is sufficient.

findings.what: The "first letter of the title, uppercased" avatar-initials helper is written eight times, and four of the copies index by UTF-16 unit instead of by composed character. Broken copies: `NSString *initials = title.length ? [title substringToIndex:1] : @"?";` at TGChatListViewController.m:2751, TGForwardPicker.m:627, TGStickersViewController.m:1685, TGChatViewController.m:2509, plus -initialsForName: (TGSettingsViewController.m:356-360), -initialsForTitle: (TGFoldersViewController.m:773-777) and -initialsForName: (TGInviteLinksViewController.m:599-610). Correct copies that use rangeOfComposedCharacterSequenceAtIndex:0 exist at TGCallViewController.m:182-187, TGTopicsViewController.m:72-77 and TGEventsInitials (TGChatEventsViewController.m:93-108).
findings.failure: A chat whose title starts with an emoji or any non-BMP character (extremely common for Telegram groups and channels, e.g. "\U0001F525 Deals") hits substringToIndex:1, which cuts the surrogate pair in half. The placeholder avatar in the chat list, the forward picker and the sticker-set list draws a lone unpaired high surrogate: a blank or replacement glyph instead of a letter. The same chat drawn by TGTopicsViewController or TGCallViewController shows the emoji correctly, so the same conversation has two different placeholder avatars in the same app.
findings.fix: Add one helper next to the drawing code it feeds, e.g. `+ (NSString *)initialsForTitle:(NSString *)title` on TGIcons (declared in TGIcons.h beside +avatarWithInitials:size:colourId:), implemented with the TGEventsInitials body from TGChatEventsViewController.m:93-108 (composed-character-sequence, up to two words, @"?" fallback). Replace all eight sites with a call to it; note TGFoldersViewController.m:775 currently falls back to @"#" and TGSettingsViewController.m:358 to @"T" for the empty case, so pass those through explicitly if the difference is wanted.

findings.what: TGDateUtils (src/TGDateUtils.mm, a port of the original 2013 client's date code) exists specifically to answer the device's 12h/24h setting - it computes value_dateHas12hFormat at TGDateUtils.mm:34 and exposes it as TGUse12hDateFormat() (TGDateUtils.mm:56-60) and +stringForShortTime:. Only three files use it (TGDateLabel.m, TGChatEventsViewController.m, TGSavedMessagesTagsViewController.m). Sixteen other files roll their own NSDateFormatter, and the message-clock ones hardcode a 24-hour pattern: `[hm setDateFormat:@"HH:mm"]` at TGChatViewController.m:4202, again at 4963 and 4989, and `[time setDateFormat:@"HH:mm"]` with an en_US_POSIX locale at TGChatListViewController.m:2165.
findings.failure: On a device whose region/locale uses a 12-hour clock (US default), every message timestamp in a bubble (-stampFor:, TGChatViewController.m:4200) and every chat-list row younger than 24h (TGChatDate, TGChatListViewController.m:2155) reads "14:05" instead of "2:05 PM", while the pinned-message date label and the chat-events screen - which do go through TGDateUtils - correctly read "2:05 PM" on the very same screen. The en_US_POSIX locale pinned at TGChatListViewController.m:2164 makes this permanent regardless of user setting.
findings.fix: Replace the bodies of -stampFor: (TGChatViewController.m:4200-4210), the two other HH:mm formatters (TGChatViewController.m:4963, 4989) and the `time` branch of TGChatDate (TGChatListViewController.m:2163-2171) with `[TGDateUtils stringForShortTime:(int)date]`. Keep the weekday/full formatters in TGChatDate but drop the hardcoded en_US_POSIX locale so they follow the device, or route them through +stringForDialogTime: which already implements the same today/this-week/older cascade.

findings.what: +avatarWithInitials:size:colourId: (TGIcons.m:849-901) does a full offscreen render every call - UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions, a rounded-rect fill, a clipped ellipse highlight and a -drawAtPoint:withFont: - and unlike +iconNamed:draw: (TGIcons.m:46-84) it never touches the sCache dictionary. One caller noticed and built a private cache: -avatarForUser:name: (TGChatViewController.m:2503-2515) memoises into self.senderAvatars, with the comment at 2501 "drawing it every row would re-download and re-decode on every scroll". The other callers did not: TGChatListViewController.m:2752, TGForwardPicker.m:628, TGStickersViewController.m:1686, TGSavedMessagesViewController.m:615, TGInviteLinksViewController.m:579, TGTopicsViewController.m:988, TGSettingsViewController.m:299 and :383 all call it straight from -tableView:cellForRowAtIndexPath: or a refresh path.
findings.failure: Scrolling the chat list on the iPhone 4S: every visible row without a downloaded photo triggers a fresh 60x60 @2x CGBitmapContext allocation, a bezier fill, a clip+ellipse and a text draw, on the main thread inside cellForRow. At ~8 visible rows and 60 reuse events per second of flick scrolling that is hundreds of offscreen contexts per second on one A5 core, which is exactly the stutter TGChatViewController.m:2501 documents avoiding.
findings.fix: Give TGIcons a bounded cache for placeholders: key on [NSString stringWithFormat:@"av-%@-%d-%d-%d", initials, (int)size, (int)(llabs(colourId) % 7), (int)[TGTheme shared].isFlat] in an NSCache with countLimit ~64 (NSCache, not the unbounded sCache dictionary at TGIcons.m:4, so it drops under memory pressure), return the hit before the UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions at line 867, and store before the return at line 900. Then delete the now-redundant self.senderAvatars placeholder memoisation in TGChatViewController.m:2506-2513 (keep the downloaded-photo half).

findings.what: Two producers build the 'chat summary' dictionary that the UI consumes, with contradictory conventions and disjoint key sets. TGClient.m:2305-2308 sets only `info[@"isGroup"] = @(![chatType isEqualToString:@"chatTypePrivate"] && ![chatType isEqualToString:@"chatTypeSecret"])` - so a channel is isGroup=YES - and never writes @"isChannel" or @"isPrivate" at all. -tgs_summaryForChat: (TGClient+Search.m:362-401) sets isGroup=NO for a channel (line 371-373) and writes isChannel and isPrivate as separate keys (lines 393-395).
findings.failure: TGSearchViewController's chat-type tabs filter on all three keys (TGSearchViewController.m:1639-1643: `_chatTypeIndex == 1 && ![chat[@"isPrivate"] boolValue]`, `== 2 && ![chat[@"isGroup"]...]`, `== 3 && ![chat[@"isChannel"]...]`). That filter can only ever run on rows from tgs_summaryForChat. The local-search rows built from [TGClient shared].chats at TGSearchViewController.m:1336-1346 carry no isChannel/isPrivate key at all and use the opposite isGroup meaning, and -runLocalSearch applies no _chatTypeIndex check anywhere. Result: with the "Channels" or "Private Chats" tab selected, every locally-matching chat of every type still appears in the chat-hits section, while the server results below it are filtered correctly.
findings.fix: Make TGClient.m's -applyChat: write the same three keys as tgs_summaryForChat: replace lines 2305-2308 with isPrivate = (chatTypePrivate || chatTypeSecret), isChannel = (chatTypeSupergroup && type[@"is_channel"] boolValue), isGroup = (chatTypeBasicGroup || (chatTypeSupergroup && !isChannel)); check every existing reader of @"isGroup" that relied on channels being grouped in (TGChatListViewController.m:2729, 2788, 2871, 2928; AppDelegate.m:316, 437; TGForwardPicker.m:653) and change them to `isGroup || isChannel` where the old meaning was intended. Then apply the same _chatTypeIndex filter from lines 1639-1643 inside -runLocalSearch's loop (TGSearchViewController.m:1336).

findings.what: Four independent byte/megabyte formatters with four different thresholds and precisions: TGHumanSize (TGStorageViewController.m:267-275) does "%.0f KB"/"%.1f MB"/"%.2f GB" from bytes; TGMediaViewController.m:44-50 does "%.0f KB"/"%.1f MB"/"%.2f GB" from bytes with its own thresholds; TGDeviceViewController.m:46-48 does "%.1f GB"/"%.0f MB" from megabytes; TGPremiumViewController.m:389-391 does "%.0f GB"/"%.0f MB" from megabytes. TGSettingsViewController.m:850 formats a fifth way inline ("photos to %lld KB").
findings.failure: The same 1536 MB limit reads "1.5 GB" on the Device screen and "2 GB" on the Premium screen (%.0f rounds up), and the same 1,572,864-byte file reads "1.5 MB" in Storage and "1.5 MB" in Media but "1536 KB" in Settings. Nothing crashes; the numbers shown to the user for one quantity disagree between screens.
findings.fix: Promote TGHumanSize(long long bytes) from TGStorageViewController.m:267 to a shared function (declare it in TGIcons.h or a small TGFormat.h) and add a `TGHumanSizeFromMegabytes(long long mb)` wrapper that calls it with mb * 1024 * 1024. Replace TGMediaViewController.m:44-50, TGDeviceViewController.m:46-48, TGPremiumViewController.m:389-391 and TGSettingsViewController.m:850 with calls to those two.

findings.what: TGMessagePreview tests the same content type twice: `if ([ctype isEqualToString:@"messageVideoNote"]) return @"Video message";` appears at line 1640-1641 and identically again at line 1650-1651. The second copy is unreachable.
findings.failure: No runtime failure - the first branch always wins - but the duplicate is the fingerprint of the copy-paste that produced the five divergent preview tables, and it costs a string comparison on the hot chat-list rebuild path for every non-video-note message that falls through to it.
